name: UMI-Bench 1.0
summary: UMI-Bench is the first benchmark dedicated to real-world evaluation of UMI-style manipulation policies. Rather than adding tasks, it standardizes the parts of an evaluation that usually go unreported and make results incomparable: data collection, scene reset, policy execution, result logging and task analysis. The first release covers 10 tabletop tasks with roughly 20k demonstrations and 50 evaluation episodes per task, and is built local-first so a lab can run the whole protocol on its own hardware and have the result be auditable by others.
innovation: Standardizes scene reset and logging — the unglamorous steps where real-robot comparability is usually lost.
Local-first design, so reproducibility does not depend on access to shared cloud hardware.
matters: UMI data underpins a large fraction of recent manipulation work, and until now every group evaluated it its own way.
limits: Tabletop and UMI-specific by construction; not a general policy benchmark.
Reproducibility still depends on each lab owning comparable hardware.
lineage: UMI's collection standard extended to an evaluation standard, in the reproducibility spirit of RoboArena.
